expiration\n- Reason for the reservation\n\nFile reservations prevent conflicts when multiple agents work on the same codebase by signaling intent to modify specific files.\n\n---\n\n## Performance Profiler\n\nNTM includes a built-in profiler for measuring startup performance and command execution times.\n\n### Enabling Profiling\n\n```bash\n# Enable for a single command\nNTM_PROFILE=1 ntm spawn myproject --cc=2\n\n# Enable globally\nexport NTM_PROFILE=1\n```\n\n### Profile Output\n\nWhen profiling is enabled, NTM outputs timing information:\n\n```\n=== NTM Performance Profile ===\nTotal Duration: 245.32ms\nSpan Count: 12\n\nBy Phase:\n startup: 42.15ms (17.2%) [4 spans]\n config: 18.50ms ( 7.5%) [2 spans]\n command: 184.67ms (75.3%) [6 spans]\n\nTop Spans by Duration:\n 145.20ms tmux_spawn [command]\n 38.50ms config_load [startup]\n 25.30ms palette_load [config]\n 18.20ms theme_detect [startup]\n\nRecommendations:\n ℹ [startup] Consider lazy loading palette commands\n```\n\n### JSON Output\n\n```bash\nNTM_PROFILE=1 ntm --robot-status --json 2>&1 | jq '.profile'\n```\n\n### Profile Categories\n\n- **startup**: Initial loading (config, themes, icons)\n- **config**: Configuration parsing and validation\n- **command**: Actual command execution\n- **deferred**: Lazy-loaded components\n- **shutdown**: Cleanup operations\n\n### Recommendations\n\nThe profiler automatically generates recommendations based on performance data:\n- Slow startup components that could be lazy-loaded\n- Commands that exceed expected duration\n- Resource-intensive operations\n\n---\n\n## Prompt History\n\nNTM maintains a history of all prompts sent to agents, enabling replay, analysis, and debugging.\n\n### How It Works\n\nEvery prompt sent via `ntm send` or the command palette is recorded with:\n- Timestamp and unique ID\n- Session and target panes\n- Full prompt text\n- Source (CLI, palette, replay)\n- Template used (if any)\n- Success/error status\n- Execution duration\n\n### Viewing History\n\n```bash\n# Get session history via robot mode\nntm --robot-history=myproject --history-stats\n\n# Filter by time range\nntm --robot-history=myproject --since=1h\n\n# JSON output for processing\nntm --robot-history=myproject --json\n```\n\n### History Storage\n\nHistory is stored in `~/.config/ntm/history.jsonl`:\n\n```json\n{\n \"id\": \"1735830245123-a1b2c3d4\",\n \"ts\": \"2025-01-02T15:04:05Z\",\n \"session\": \"myproject\",\n \"targets\": [\"0\", \"1\", \"2\"],\n \"prompt\": \"Review the authentication implementation\",\n \"source\": \"palette\",\n \"template\": \"code_review\",\n \"success\": true,\n \"duration_ms\": 125\n}\n```\n\n### Configuration\n\n```toml\n[history]\nenabled = true\npath = \"~/.config/ntm/history.jsonl\"\nmax_entries = 10000 # Max entries to keep\nretention_days = 90 # Delete entries older than this\n```\n\n### Use Cases\n\n- **Debugging**: See exactly what was sent when an agent misbehaves\n- **Replay**: Re-send successful prompts to new sessions\n- **Analytics**: Track prompt patterns and agent usage\n- **Audit**: Review all instructions given to agents\n\n---\n\n## Work Distribution\n\nNTM integrates with bv (Beads Viewer) to provide intelligent prioritization based on dependency graph analysis. The `ntm work` commands help you prioritize tasks, identify bottlenecks, and feed assignment decisions across agents.\n\n### Triage Analysis\n\nGet a complete triage analysis with prioritized recommendations:\n\n```bash\nntm work triage # Full triage with recommendations\nntm work triage --by-label # Group by label/domain\nntm work triage --by-track # Group by execution track\nntm work triage --quick # Show only quick wins\nntm work triage --health # Include project health metrics\nntm work triage --json # Machine-readable output\n```\n\nThe triage analysis includes:\n- **Recommendations**: Ranked actionable items with impact scores\n- **Quick Wins**: Low-effort, high-impact items to tackle first\n- **Bottlenecks**: Issues blocking the most downstream work\n- **Project Health**: Status distributions, graph metrics\n\n### Alerts\n\nMonitor for drift and proactive issues:\n\n```bash\nntm work alerts # All alerts\nntm work alerts --critical-only # Only critical alerts\nntm work alerts --type=stale_issue # Filter by type\nntm work alerts --label=backend # Filter by label\n```\n\nAlert types include:\n- **Stale Issues**: Items untouched for too long\n- **Priority Drift**: Urgency mismatches vs. actual impact\n- **Blocking Cascades**: Single issues blocking many others\n- **Cycle Detection**: Circular dependencies that need breaking\n\n### Semantic Search\n\nSearch across issues and their context:\n\n```bash\nntm work search \"JWT authentication\" # Semantic search\nntm work search \"rate limiting\" -n 20 # Limit results\nntm work search \"API\" --label=backend # Filter by label\n```\n\n### Impact Analysis\n\nAnalyze the impact of specific files or changes:\n\n```bash\nntm work impact src/api/*.go # Impact of API files\nntm work impact --show-graph # Include dependency visualization\n```\n\n### Next Action\n\nGet the single best next action:\n\n```bash\nntm work next # Top recommendation + claim command\nntm work next --json # Machine-readable\n```\n\nThis returns the highest-impact, unblocked item with a ready-to-run `bd update` command to claim it.\n\n---\n\n## Intelligent Work Assignment\n\nNTM includes a sophisticated work assignment system that matches tasks to agents based on agent capabilities, task characteristics, and configurable strategies.\n\n### Canonical Assignment Flow (CLI)\n\nUse `ntm assign` to recommend or execute assignments:\n\n```bash\nntm assign myproject # Show assignment recommendations\nntm assign myproject --auto # Execute assignments without confirmation\nntm assign myproject --strategy=dependency # Prioritize unblocking work\nntm assign myproject --beads=bd-42,bd-45 # Assign specific beads only\n```\n\nSpawn and assign in one step:\n\n```bash\nntm spawn myproject --cc=2 --cod=2 --assign\nntm spawn myproject --cc=4 --assign --strategy=quality\n```\n\nAvailable strategies (shared by `ntm assign` and `ntm spawn --assign`):\n`balanced`, `speed`, `quality`, `dependency`, `round-robin`.\n\n### Agent Capability Matrix\n\nDifferent AI agents excel at different types of work. NTM maintains a capability matrix that influences assignment recommendations:\n\n| Agent | Best At | Strength Score |\n|-------|---------|----------------|\n| **Claude** | Analysis, refactoring, documentation, architecture | Analysis: 0.9, Refactor: 0.9, Docs: 0.8 |\n| **Codex** | Feature implementation, bug fixes, quick tasks | Feature: 0.9, Bug: 0.8, Task: 0.8 |\n| **Gemini** | Documentation, analysis, features | Docs: 0.9, Analysis: 0.8, Feature: 0.8 |\n\n### Task Type Inference\n\nNTM automatically infers task types from bead titles using keyword analysis:\n\n| Task Type | Keywords |\n|-----------|----------|\n| Bug | `bug`, `fix`, `broken`, `error`, `crash` |\n| Testing | `test`, `spec`, `coverage` |\n| Documentation | `doc`, `readme`, `comment`, `documentation` |\n| Refactor | `refactor`, `cleanup`, `improve`, `consolidate` |\n| Analysis | `analyze`, `investigate`, `research`, `design` |\n| Feature | `feature`, `implement`, `add`, `new` |\n\n### Assignment Strategies\n\nChoose a strategy based on your priorities:\n\n```bash\n# Balanced (default): Distribute work evenly across agents\nntm --robot-assign=myproject --strategy=balanced\n\n# Speed: Assign any available work to any idle agent quickly\nntm --robot-assign=myproject --strategy=speed\n\n# Quality: Optimize agent-task match for best results\nntm --robot-assign=myproject --strategy=quality\n\n# Dependency: Prioritize items that unblock the most downstream work\nntm --robot-assign=myproject --strategy=dependency\n```\n\n### Strategy Behavior\n\n**Balanced** (default):\n- Considers agent strengths for task types\n- Distributes work fairly across idle agents\n- Good general-purpose choice\n\n**Speed**:\n- Maximizes throughput\n- Assigns any idle agent to any ready task\n- Best when time is critical\n\n**Quality**:\n- Strictly matches agent capabilities to task types\n- May leave agents idle if no suitable tasks\n- Best for complex, high-stakes work\n\n**Dependency**:\n- Prioritizes high-priority items (P0, P1)\n- Focuses on unblocking downstream work\n- Best for projects with deep dependency graphs\n\n### Assignment Output\n\n```bash\nntm --robot-assign=myproject\n```\n\nReturns recommendations with confidence scores:\n\n```json\n{\n \"success\": true,\n \"session\": \"myproject\",\n \"strategy\": \"balanced\",\n \"recommendations\": [\n {\n \"agent\": \"1\",\n \"agent_type\": \"claude\",\n \"model\": \"sonnet\",\n \"assign_bead\": \"bd-42\",\n \"bead_title\": \"Refactor authentication module\",\n \"priority\": \"P1\",\n \"confidence\": 0.9,\n \"reasoning\": \"claude excels at refactor tasks; high priority\"\n }\n ],\n \"idle_agents\": [\"1\", \"2\", \"4\"],\n \"summary\": {\n \"total_agents\": 5,\n \"idle_agents\": 3,\n \"ready_beads\": 8,\n \"recommendations\": 3\n },\n \"_agent_hints\": {\n \"summary\": \"3 assignments recommended for 3 idle agents\",\n \"suggested_commands\": [\n \"bd update bd-42 --assignee=pane1\",\n \"bd update bd-45 --assignee=pane2\"\n ]\n }\n}\n```\n\n### Filtering Assignments\n\n```bash\n# Assign specific beads only\nntm --robot-assign=myproject --beads=bd-42,bd-45\n\n# Combine with strategy\nntm --robot-assign=myproject --strategy=quality --beads=bd-42\n```\n\n### Integration with Agent Mail\n\nWhen using Agent Mail for multi-agent coordination, file reservations are automatically considered:\n\n1. Beads that require files already reserved by another agent are marked as conflicts\n2. Assignment recommendations include warnings about potential conflicts\n3. Agents can be configured to auto-claim file reservations when assigned work\n\n---\n\n## Safety System\n\nNTM includes a safety system that blocks or warns about dangerous commands that could cause data loss or other irreversible damage. This is particularly important when AI agents are running autonomously.\n\n### Protected Commands\n\nThe safety system recognizes dangerous patterns including:\n\n| Pattern | Risk | Action |\n|---------|------|--------|\n| `git reset --hard` | Loses uncommitted changes | Block |\n| `git push --force` | Overwrites remote history | Block |\n| `rm -rf /` | Catastrophic deletion | Block |\n| `git clean -fd` | Deletes untracked files | Approval required |\n| `DROP TABLE` | Database destruction | Block |\n\n### Status and Configuration\n\n```bash\nntm safety status # Show protection status\nntm safety blocked # View blocked command history\nntm safety blocked --hours=24 # Blocked commands in last 24h\nntm safety check \"git reset --hard HEAD~1\" # Test a command\n```\n\n### Installation\n\nInstall safety wrappers and hooks:\n\n```bash\nntm safety install # Install git wrapper + Claude hook\nntm safety install --force # Overwrite existing\nntm safety uninstall # Remove all safety components\n```\n\nWhen installed, the safety system:\n1. **Git Wrapper**: Intercepts dangerous git commands before execution\n2. **Claude Hook**: Integrates with Claude Code's PreToolUse hooks\n3. **Policy Engine**: Evaluates commands against configurable rules\n\n### Custom Policy\n\nCreate a custom policy in `~/.ntm/policy.yaml`:\n\n```yaml\nrules:\n - pattern: \"rm -rf ${HOME}\"\n action: block\n reason: \"Prevents accidental home directory deletion\"\n\n - pattern: \"git push.*--force\"\n action: approval\n reason: \"Force push requires explicit confirmation\"\n\n - pattern: \"npm publish\"\n action: approval\n reason: \"Publishing requires review\"\n```\n\nActions:\n- **block**: Immediately reject the command\n- **approval**: Require explicit confirmation\n- **warn**: Log a warning but allow execution\n- **allow**: Explicitly permit (overrides default rules)\n\n### Policy Management\n\n```bash\nntm policy show # Display current policy\nntm policy show --all # Include default rules\nntm policy validate # Check policy syntax\nntm policy reset # Reset to defaults\nntm policy edit # Open in $EDITOR\n```\n\n---\n\n## Privacy & Redaction\n\nNTM scans prompts and outputs for secrets/PII at critical IO boundaries (send/copy/save/mail/export) and supports a privacy mode for sessions that should not persist data. The canonical redaction engine lives in `internal/redaction` and is documented in `docs/REDACTION_SPEC.md`.\n\n### Redaction Modes\n\nRedaction can be controlled per-command with `--redact=off|warn|redact|block` or in config via `redaction.mode`.\n\n- `off`: no scanning or redaction.\n- `warn`: detect secrets and emit warnings without changing content.\n- `redact`: replace matches with placeholders like `[REDACTED:OPENAI_KEY:deadbeef]`.\n- `block`: fail the operation when secrets are detected.\n\nExamples (synthetic secrets only):\n\n```bash\nntm send myproject --redact=warn --cc \"Use sk-proj-FAKEtestkey1234567890123456789012345678901234 for testing\"\nntm send myproject --redact=block --all \"token=ghp_FAKEtesttokenvalue12345678901234567\"\nntm send myproject --redact=block --allow-secret --all \"token=ghp_FAKEtesttokenvalue12345678901234567\"\n```\n\n`--allow-secret` downgrades `block` to `warn` for a single invocation (use with caution).\n\n### Prompt Preflight\n\nUse `ntm preflight` to lint prompts and run secret detection before dispatching:\n\n```bash\nntm preflight \"Review auth changes in src/auth.go\"\nntm preflight --strict \"rm -rf /tmp/cache\"\nntm preflight --json \"Deploy with token=ghp_FAKEtesttokenvalue12345678901234567\"\n```\n\n`--strict` treats warnings as failures, making it safe to enforce in automation.\n\n### Privacy Mode\n\nPrivacy mode disables persistence of sensitive session data (prompt history, event logs, checkpoints, scrollback capture). Enable per session:\n\n```bash\nntm spawn myproject --cc=2 --privacy\n```\n\nOverride for a single command when you explicitly want to persist or export:\n\n```bash\nntm support-bundle myproject --allow-persist\n```\n\nPrivacy defaults can be set in config:\n\n```toml\n[redaction]\nmode = \"warn\"\nallowlist = [\"^dev-\"]\n\n[privacy]\nenabled = false\ndisable_prompt_history = true\ndisable_event_logs = true\ndisable_checkpoints = true\ndisable_scrollback_capture = true\nrequire_explicit_persist = true\n```\n\n### Scrub Artifacts\n\nScan NTM artifacts without leaking raw secrets:\n\n```bash\nntm scrub --path .ntm --format json\n```\n\n---\n\n## Configuration Management\n\nNTM provides commands for inspecting and managing your configuration.\n\n### Viewing Configuration\n\n```bash\nntm config show # Display effective configuration\nntm config show --json # JSON output\n```\n\n### Comparing with Defaults\n\nSee what you've customized:\n\n```bash\nntm config diff # Show differences from defaults\nntm config diff --json # Machine-readable diff\n```\n\nExample output:\n```\nConfiguration differences from defaults:\n\n projects_base: ~/Developer (default: /data/projects)\n tmux.default_panes: 12 (default: 10)\n context_rotation.warning_threshold: 0.85 (default: 0.8)\n```\n\n### Validation\n\nCheck your configuration for errors:\n\n```bash\nntm config validate # Validate current config\nntm config validate --json # Machine-readable output\n```\n\nValidation checks:\n- Syntax errors in TOML\n- Invalid threshold values (e.g., > 1.0 for percentages)\n- Missing required fields\n- Path existence for critical directories\n- Agent command validity\n\n### Getting Specific Values\n\nRetrieve individual configuration values:\n\n```bash\nntm config get projects_base # Get single value\nntm config get context_rotation.warning_threshold\nntm config get agents.claude # Get agent command\nntm config get --json # All config as JSON\n```\n\n### Editing Configuration\n\n```bash\nntm config edit # Open in $EDITOR\n```\n\n### Reset to Defaults\n\n```bash\nntm config reset # Requires --confirm\nntm config reset --confirm # Actually reset\n```\n\n---\n\n## Pipeline Workflows\n\nNTM supports YAML-defined workflows for complex multi-step operations. Pipelines can orchestrate agents, run commands, and manage dependencies.\n\n### Defining a Pipeline\n\nCreate `.ntm/pipelines/` or use built-in pipelines:\n\n```yaml\n# .ntm/pipelines/review.yaml\nname: code-review\ndescription: Comprehensive code review workflow\n\nvariables:\n branch: main\n\nsteps:\n - id: fetch\n name: Fetch latest changes\n command: git fetch origin ${branch}\n\n - id: analyze\n name: Static analysis\n command: ubs .\n continue_on_error: true\n\n - id: review\n name: AI code review\n agent: claude\n prompt: |\n Review the changes in this branch. Focus on:\n 1. Security vulnerabilities\n 2. Performance issues\n 3. Code quality\n depends_on: [fetch, analyze]\n\n - id: tests\n name: Run tests\n command: go test ./...\n parallel: true\n depends_on: [fetch]\n\n - id: summary\n name: Generate summary\n agent: claude\n prompt: \"Summarize the review findings and test results.\"\n depends_on: [review, tests]\n```\n\n### Running Pipelines\n\n```bash\nntm pipeline run review # Run the review pipeline\nntm pipeline run review --dry-run # Show what would happen\nntm pipeline run review --var branch=dev # Override variables\nntm pipeline run review --stage=analyze # Run specific stage only\n```\n\n### Pipeline Commands\n\n```bash\nntm pipeline list # List available pipelines\nntm pipeline status # Show running pipelines\nntm pipeline status --watch # Live status updates\nntm pipeline cancel # Cancel a running pipeline\n```\n\n### Step Types\n\n| Type | Description |\n|------|-------------|\n| `command` | Shell command execution |\n| `agent` | Send prompt to AI agent |\n| `parallel` | Run steps in parallel |\n| `loop` | Iterate over items |\n| `conditional` | Execute based on condition |\n\n### Dependency Resolution\n\nPipelines use topological sorting to resolve dependencies:\n- Steps with `depends_on` wait for dependencies\n- Independent steps can run in parallel\n- Cycle detection prevents infinite loops\n\n---\n\n## Session Checkpoints\n\nCheckpoints capture the complete state of a tmux session at a point in time, enabling rollback and recovery.\n\n### Creating Checkpoints\n\n```bash\n# Create a checkpoint\nntm checkpoint save myproject\n\n# With description\nntm checkpoint save myproject -m \"Before major refactor\"\n\n# Custom scrollback depth\nntm checkpoint save myproject --scrollback=500\n\n# Skip git state capture\nntm checkpoint save myproject --no-git\n```\n\n**Captured Data:**\n- Pane layout and configuration\n- Agent types and commands\n- Scrollback buffer content (configurable depth)\n- Git repository state (branch, commit, uncommitted changes)\n- Working directory\n\n### Listing Checkpoints\n\n```bash\n# List all checkpoints across sessions\nntm checkpoint list\n\n# List checkpoints for a specific session\nntm checkpoint list myproject\n\n# JSON output\nntm checkpoint list --json\n```\n\n### Viewing Checkpoint Details\n\n```bash\nntm checkpoint show myproject 20251210-143052\nntm checkpoint show myproject 20251210-143052 --json\n```\n\n**Displayed Information:**\n- Creation timestamp\n- Pane count and agent types\n- Git branch and commit\n- Dirty status (staged/unstaged/untracked counts)\n- Description (if provided)\n\n### Deleting Checkpoints\n\n```bash\n# Interactive deletion\nntm checkpoint delete myproject 20251210-143052\n\n# Force delete without confirmation\nntm checkpoint delete myproject 20251210-143052 --force\n```\n\n### Auto-Checkpoints\n\nNTM automatically creates checkpoints before risky operations:\n- Broadcasting prompts to multiple agents\n- Adding or removing agents from a session\n- Spawning new sessions with agent configurations\n- Operations flagged as potentially destructive\n\nThis provides automatic rollback points without manual intervention.\n\n### Storage Location\n\nCheckpoints are stored in `~/.local/share/ntm/checkpoints/` organized by session name. Each checkpoint includes:\n- `checkpoint.json` - Metadata and session configuration\n- `panes/*.txt` - Scrollback content for each pane\n- `git.patch` - Uncommitted changes (if any)\n\n---\n\n## Session Persistence\n\nSave and restore complete session state, including agent configurations, prompts, and context.\n\n### Saving Sessions\n\n```bash\nntm sessions save myproject # Save current state\nntm sessions save myproject --name=\"pre-refactor\" # Named snapshot\nntm sessions save myproject --include-history # Include prompt history\n```\n\nSaved state includes:\n- Agent pane configuration (types, counts)\n- Current working directories\n- Recent prompts (optional)\n- Checkpoint references\n- Custom metadata\n\n### Listing Saved Sessions\n\n```bash\nntm sessions list # List all saved sessions\nntm sessions list --json # Machine-readable\n```\n\n### Viewing Session Details\n\n```bash\nntm sessions show myproject # Show latest save\nntm sessions show myproject --name=\"pre-refactor\" # Specific snapshot\n```\n\n### Restoring Sessions\n\n```bash\nntm sessions restore myproject # Restore latest\nntm sessions restore myproject --name=\"pre-refactor\" # Specific snapshot\nntm sessions restore myproject --dry-run # Preview what would happen\n```\n\n### Deleting Saved Sessions\n\n```bash\nntm sessions delete myproject --name=\"old-snapshot\"\nntm sessions delete myproject --all --force # Delete all snapshots\n```\n\n---\n\n## Recipes\n\nRecipes are predefined operation sequences for common tasks. They combine multiple NTM commands into a single workflow.\n\n### Available Recipes\n\n```bash\nntm recipes list # List all recipes\nntm recipes list --category=setup # Filter by category\nntm recipes show morning-standup # Show recipe details\n```\n\n### Built-in Recipes\n\n| Recipe | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| `morning-standup` | Start day: sync git, triage work, spawn agents |\n| `code-review` | Full review cycle: analyze, review, test |\n| `context-recovery` | Recover from compaction: re-read AGENTS.md, get beads context |\n| `end-of-day` | Save state, commit changes, push, kill session |\n| `fresh-start` | Kill session, clean state, respawn |\n\n### Running Recipes\n\n```bash\nntm recipes run morning-standup myproject\nntm recipes run code-review myproject --dry-run\n```\n\n### Custom Recipes\n\nDefine custom recipes in `~/.config/ntm/recipes.yaml`:\n\n```yaml\nrecipes:\n - name: my-deploy\n description: Deploy to staging\n category: deployment\n steps:\n - command: ntm send ${session} --all \"Stop current work, we're deploying\"\n - command: git push origin staging\n - command: ntm send ${session} --cc \"Monitor deployment logs\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Prompt Templates\n\nNTM includes a built-in template system for common prompting patterns, reducing repetitive typing and ensuring consistent agent interactions.\n\n### Built-in Templates\n\n| Template | Description |\n|----------|-------------|\n| `code_review` | Review code for quality, bugs, performance, and security issues |\n| `explain` | Walk through code with control flow analysis |\n| `refactor` | Improve structure, naming conventions, and simplification |\n| `test` | Generate comprehensive test coverage |\n| `document` | Add documentation (JSDoc, GoDoc, docstring styles) |\n| `fix` | Fix specific issues with root cause analysis |\n| `implement` | Implement features or functions from specifications |\n| `optimize` | Optimize for time complexity, memory, or both |\n\n### Using Templates\n\n```bash\n# Use a template with ntm send\nntm send myproject --cc --template code_review\n\n# With custom variables\nntm send myproject --cc --template fix --var issue=\"null pointer exception\"\n\n# List available templates\nntm templates list\n\n# Show template content\nntm templates show code_review\n```\n\n### Variable Substitution\n\nTemplates support variable substitution with defaults:\n\n```\nReview {{file|main.go}} for {{focus|all issues}}\n```\n\n**Built-in Variables:**\n- `{{cwd}}` - Current working directory\n- `{{date}}` - Current date (YYYY-MM-DD)\n- `{{time}}` - Current time (HH:MM:SS)\n- `{{session}}` - Active session name\n- `{{clipboard}}` - Clipboard contents (if available)\n\n### Conditional Sections\n\nTemplates support Mustache-style conditionals:\n\n```\n{{#has_tests}}\nAlso update the test file at {{test_file}}.\n{{/has_tests}}\n```\n\n### Template Sources\n\nTemplates are loaded from three locations (later sources override earlier):\n\n1. **Built-in**: Compiled into NTM\n2. **User**: `~/.config/ntm/templates/`\n3. **Project**: `.ntm/templates/`\n\n### Custom Templates\n\nCreate custom templates in `~/.config/ntm/templates/my-template.txt`:\n\n```\nYou are reviewing {{language|Go}} code.\n\nFocus on:\n- Error handling\n- Edge cases\n- Performance implications\n\n{{#context}}\nAdditional context: {{context}}\n{{/context}}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Ensembles: Validation Rules and Examples\n\nEnsemble presets live in `~/.config/ntm/ensembles.toml` (user) and `.ntm/ensembles.toml` (project). Validation runs when presets are loaded or when you spawn an ensemble. Errors reference the exact field path.\n\n### Minimal valid example\n\n```toml\n[[ensembles]]\nname = \"project-diagnosis\"\ndisplay_name = \"Project Diagnosis\"\ndescription = \"Baseline health review\"\nmodes = [\n { id = \"deductive\" },\n { code = \"A7\" }, # resolves to \"type-theoretic\"\n]\nallow_advanced = false\n\n[synthesis]\nstrategy = \"consensus\"\n\n[budget]\nmax_tokens_per_mode = 4000\nmax_total_tokens = 50000\nsynthesis_reserve_tokens = 5000\ncontext_reserve_tokens = 5000\n```\n\n### Mode refs: id vs code\n\n- `id` must be lowercase and match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`.\n- `code` must match `[A-L][0-9]+` (e.g., `A4`) and is resolved to a mode id.\n- Exactly one of `id` or `code` is required.\n\nInvalid examples and actual messages:\n\n```toml\nmodes = [{ id = \"deductive\", code = \"A1\" }]\n```\n```\nmodes[0]: mode ref must specify id or code, not both\n```\n\n```toml\nmodes = [{}]\n```\n```\nmodes[0]: mode ref must specify either id or code\n```\n\n```toml\nmodes = [{ code = \"Z9\" }]\n```\n```\nmodes[0]: invalid mode code \"Z9\"\n```\n\n### Valid/invalid preset examples\n\n```toml\n[[ensembles]]\nname = \"Project Diagnosis\"\ndescription = \"Bad preset name + single mode\"\nmodes = [{ id = \"deductive\" }]\n```\n```\nname: invalid mode ID \"Project Diagnosis\": must be lowercase, start with a letter, and contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens\nmodes: mode count must be between 2 and 10 (got 1)\n```\n\n### Strategy compatibility (manual/voting/argumentation-graph)\n\nSupported strategies:\n`manual`, `voting` (no synthesizer agent) and\n`adversarial`, `consensus`, `creative`, `analytical`, `deliberative`, `prioritized`,\n`dialectical`, `meta-reasoning`, `argumentation-graph` (require a synthesizer mode).\n\nDeprecated or unknown strategy examples:\n\n```toml\n[synthesis]\nstrategy = \"debate\"\n```\n```\nstrategy \"debate\" is deprecated; use \"dialectical\" instead\n```\n\n```toml\n[synthesis]\nstrategy = \"mystery\"\n```\n```\nunknown synthesis strategy \"mystery\"; use ListStrategies() for valid options\n```\n\nNotes:\n- `argumentation-graph` uses a synthesizer mode named `argumentation`.\n- If the synthesizer mode is missing from the catalog you will see:\n `synthesis.strategy: synthesizer mode \"argumentation\" not found in catalog`.\n\n### Streaming synthesis output\n\nYou can stream incremental synthesis chunks:\n\n```bash\nntm ensemble synthesize mysession --stream\nntm ensemble synthesize mysession --stream --format json # JSONL chunks\nntm ensemble synthesize mysession --stream --resume --run-id \n```\n\nNotes:\n- `--stream --format json` emits one JSON object per line (JSONL).\n- On Ctrl+C, NTM writes a synthesis checkpoint and prints a resume command.\n\n### Budget validation\n\n```toml\n[budget]\nmax_tokens_per_mode = 60000\nmax_total_tokens = 20000\nsynthesis_reserve_tokens = 15000\ncontext_reserve_tokens = 10000\n```\n```\nbudget.max_tokens_per_mode: per-mode budget exceeds total budget\nbudget: reserved tokens exceed total budget\n```\n\n```toml\n[budget]\nmax_total_tokens = -1\n```\n```\nbudget: budget values must be non-negative\n```\n\nUpper bounds enforced:\n- `budget.max_tokens_per_mode: per-mode budget exceeds reasonable upper bound (200000)`\n- `budget.max_total_tokens: total budget exceeds reasonable upper bound (1000000)`\n\n### Extension chains and circular detection\n\n```toml\n[[ensembles]]\nname = \"child\"\nextends = \"missing\"\ndescription = \"Missing parent\"\nmodes = [{ id = \"deductive\" }, { id = \"type-theoretic\" }]\n```\n```\nextends: extended preset \"missing\" not found\n```\n\n```toml\n[[ensembles]]\nname = \"a\"\nextends = \"b\"\ndescription = \"Cycle A\"\nmodes = [{ id = \"deductive\" }, { id = \"type-theoretic\" }]\n\n[[ensembles]]\nname = \"b\"\nextends = \"a\"\ndescription = \"Cycle B\"\nmodes = [{ id = \"deductive\" }, { id = \"type-theoretic\" }]\n```\n```\npresets.a.extends: circular extension detected\n```\n\nExtension depth is capped at 3:\n```\npresets.child.extends: extension depth exceeds 3\n```\n\n### Tier gating (advanced/experimental)\n\n```toml\n[[ensembles]]\nname = \"advanced-demo\"\ndescription = \"Uses an advanced mode\"\nmodes = [{ id = \"equational\" }, { id = \"deductive\" }]\nallow_advanced = false\n```\n```\nmodes[0]: mode \"equational\" is tier \"advanced\" but allow_advanced is false\n```\n\nSet `allow_advanced = true` to include advanced/experimental modes.\n\n---\n\n## Workflow Templates\n\nWorkflow templates define multi-agent coordination patterns for common development workflows. They specify which agents to spawn, how they interact, and when to transition between workflow stages.\n\n### Built-in Templates\n\n| Template | Coordination | Agents | Description |\n|----------|--------------|--------|-------------|\n| `red-green` | ping-pong | tester, implementer | TDD workflow: write failing tests, then make them pass |\n| `review-pipeline` | review-gate | implementer, 2× reviewer | Code with mandatory review before finalization |\n| `specialist-team` | pipeline | architect, 2× implementer, tester | Design → Build → QA pipeline |\n| `parallel-explore` | parallel | 3× explorer | Multiple agents explore different approaches simultaneously |\n\n### Template Commands\n\n```bash\nntm workflows list # List all available templates\nntm workflows show red-green # Show detailed template info\nntm workflows list --json # JSON output for scripts\n```\n\n### Template Sources\n\nTemplates are loaded from three locations (later sources override earlier):\n\n1. **Built-in**: Compiled into NTM (lowest priority)\n2. **User**: `~/.config/ntm/workflows/` (overrides built-in)\n3. **Project**: `.ntm/workflows/` (highest priority)\n\n### Coordination Types\n\n| Type | Icon | Description |\n|------|------|-------------|\n| `ping-pong` | ⇄ | Alternating work between agents (e.g., TDD red-green) |\n| `pipeline` | → | Sequential stages with handoff (e.g., design → build → qa) |\n| `parallel` | ≡ | Simultaneous independent work |\n| `review-gate` | ✓ | Work with approval gates |\n\n### Creating Custom Templates\n\nCreate `~/.config/ntm/workflows/my-workflow.toml` or `.ntm/workflows/my-workflow.toml`:\n\n```toml\n[[workflows]]\nname = \"my-workflow\"\ndescription = \"Custom workflow description\"\ncoordination = \"ping-pong\"\n\n[[workflows.agents]]\nprofile = \"implementer\"\nrole = \"coder\"\ndescription = \"Writes the implementation\"\n\n[[workflows.agents]]\nprofile = \"reviewer\"\nrole = \"checker\"\ndescription = \"Reviews and suggests improvements\"\n\n[workflows.flow]\ninitial = \"coder\"\n\n[[workflows.flow.transitions]]\nfrom = \"coder\"\nto = \"checker\"\n[workflows.flow.transitions.trigger]\ntype = \"manual\"\nlabel = \"Ready for review\"\n\n[[workflows.flow.transitions]]\nfrom = \"checker\"\nto = \"coder\"\n[workflows.flow.transitions.trigger]\ntype = \"agent_says\"\npattern = \"changes requested\"\nrole = \"checker\"\n```\n\n### Trigger Types\n\nTransitions between workflow stages can be triggered by:\n\n| Trigger | Parameters | Description |\n|---------|------------|-------------|\n| `file_created` | `pattern` | File matching glob pattern is created |\n| `file_modified` | `pattern` | File matching glob pattern is modified |\n| `command_success` | `command` | Shell command exits successfully |\n| `command_failure` | `command` | Shell command fails |\n| `agent_says` | `pattern`, `role` | Agent output matches regex pattern |\n| `all_agents_idle` | `idle_minutes` | All agents idle for specified time |\n| `manual` | `label` | Manual trigger via UI or command |\n| `time_elapsed` | `minutes` | Fixed time delay |\n\n### Error Handling\n\nConfigure how the workflow responds to errors:\n\n```toml\n[workflows.error_handling]\non_agent_crash = \"restart_agent\" # restart_agent, pause, skip_stage, abort, notify\non_agent_error = \"pause\"\non_timeout = \"notify\"\nstage_timeout_minutes = 30\nmax_retries_per_stage = 2\n```\n\n### Example: Red-Green TDD Workflow\n\n```toml\n[[workflows]]\nname = \"red-green\"\ndescription = \"Test-Driven Development: write failing tests, then make them pass\"\ncoordination = \"ping-pong\"\n\n[[workflows.agents]]\nprofile = \"tester\"\nrole = \"red\"\ndescription = \"Writes failing tests that define expected behavior\"\n\n[[workflows.agents]]\nprofile = \"implementer\"\nrole = \"green\"\ndescription = \"Implements code to make tests pass\"\n\n[workflows.flow]\ninitial = \"red\"\n\n[[workflows.flow.transitions]]\nfrom = \"red\"\nto = \"green\"\n[workflows.flow.transitions.trigger]\ntype = \"file_created\"\npattern = \"*_test.go\"\n\n[[workflows.flow.transitions]]\nfrom = \"green\"\nto = \"red\"\n[workflows.flow.transitions.trigger]\ntype = \"command_success\"\ncommand = \"go test ./...\"\n\n[[workflows.prompts]]\nkey = \"feature\"\nquestion = \"What feature are you implementing?\"\nrequired = true\n\n[workflows.error_handling]\non_agent_error = \"pause\"\nstage_timeout_minutes = 30\n```\n\n---\n\n## Agent Resilience\n\nNTM monitors agent health and can automatically recover from crashes, rate limits, and other failures.\n\n### Auto-Restart\n\nWhen enabled, NTM automatically restarts crashed agents:\n\n```toml\n[resilience]\nauto_restart = true # Enable auto-restart (opt-in)\nmax_restarts = 3 # Max restarts before giving up\nrestart_delay_seconds = 30 # Delay between restart attempts\nhealth_check_seconds = 10 # Health check interval\nnotify_on_crash = true # Desktop notification on crash\nnotify_on_max_restarts = true # Notify when max restarts exceeded\n```\n\n### Rate Limit Detection\n\nNTM detects rate limit messages and can trigger account rotation:\n\n```toml\n[resilience.rate_limit]\ndetect = true # Enable rate limit detection\nnotify = true # Notify when rate limited\nauto_rotate = false # Trigger account rotation\npatterns = [ # Custom detection patterns\n \"rate limit exceeded\",\n \"too many requests\"\n]\n```\n\n### Health Monitoring\n\nEach agent tracks:\n- Restart count since session start\n- Current health status (healthy, warning, error)\n- Rate limit state\n- Last activity timestamp\n\nView health status:\n\n```bash\nntm health myproject # Check all agent health\nntm health myproject --json # Programmatic access\n```\n\n---\n\n## Notification System\n\nNTM can send notifications for important events through multiple channels.\n\n### Event Types\n\n| Event | Description |\n|-------|-------------|\n| `agent.error` | Agent entered error state |\n| `agent.crashed` | Agent process exited unexpectedly |\n| `agent.restarted` | Agent was automatically restarted |\n| `agent.idle` | Agent waiting for input |\n| `agent.rate_limit` | Rate limit detected |\n| `rotation.needed` | Account rotation recommended |\n| `session.created` | New session spawned |\n| `session.killed` | Session terminated |\n| `health.degraded` | Overall health dropped |\n\n### Notification Channels\n\n**Desktop Notifications:**\n\n```toml\n[notifications]\nenabled = true\nchannels = [\"desktop\"]\n\n[notifications.desktop]\nenabled = true\n# Uses osascript on macOS, notify-send on Linux\n```\n\n**Webhook:**\n\n```toml\n[notifications.webhook]\nenabled = true\nurl = \"https://hooks.slack.com/services/...\"\nmethod = \"POST\"\ntemplate = '''\n{\n \"text\": \"NTM: {{.Type}} - {{.Message}}\"\n}\n'''\n```\n\n**Shell Command:**\n\n```toml\n[notifications.shell]\nenabled = true\ncommand = \"my-notifier\"\n# Receives JSON on stdin with event details\n# Environment: NTM_EVENT_TYPE, NTM_EVENT_MESSAGE, NTM_SESSION\n```\n\n**Log File:**\n\n```toml\n[notifications.log]\nenabled = true\npath = \"~/.config/ntm/notifications.log\"\n# Append-only logging of all events\n```\n\n### Event Filtering\n\n```toml\n[notifications]\nevents = [\"agent.crashed\", \"agent.rate_limit\", \"health.degraded\"]\n# Only receive notifications for these events\n```\n\n---\n\n## Token Estimation\n\nNTM estimates token usage to help manage context windows and prevent exhaustion.\n\n### Content-Aware Estimation\n\nToken estimation varies by content type:\n\n| Content Type | Chars/Token | Rationale |\n|--------------|-------------|-----------|\n| Code | 2.8 | More punctuation, operators |\n| JSON | 3.0 | Structured, repetitive |\n| Markdown | 3.5 | Mixed content |\n| Prose | 4.0 | Natural language |\n\n### Context Limits\n\nBuilt-in limits for popular models:\n\n| Model | Context Limit |\n|-------|---------------|\n| Claude (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) | 200,000 tokens |\n| GPT-4 / GPT-4o | 128,000 tokens |\n| Gemini (Pro/Flash/Ultra) | 1,000,000 tokens |\n\n### Usage Monitoring\n\n```bash\n# View context usage for all agents\nntm --robot-context=myproject\n\n# JSON output for automation\nntm --robot-context=myproject --json\n```\n\n### Overhead Estimation\n\nSystem prompts and conversation history add overhead:\n\n| Factor | Multiplier |\n|--------|------------|\n| System prompt | 1.2x |\n| Conversation history | 1.5x |\n| Tool usage | 2.0x |\n\n---\n\n## Account Rotation\n\nFor high-volume usage, NTM supports rotating between multiple accounts to avoid rate limits.\n\n### Configuration\n\n```toml\n[rotation]\nenabled = true\nprefer_restart = true # Restart agent vs in-pane reauth\nauto_open_browser = false # Auto-open auth URLs\nauto_trigger = false # Automatic rotation on rate limit\ncontinuation_prompt = \"Continue where you left off. Previous context...\"\n\n[[rotation.accounts]]\nprovider = \"claude\"\nemail = \"primary@example.com\"\nalias = \"main\"\npriority = 1 # Lower = higher priority\n\n[[rotation.accounts]]\nprovider = \"claude\"\nemail = \"backup@example.com\"\nalias = \"backup\"\npriority = 2\n```\n\n### Provider-Specific Authentication\n\n| Provider | Method | Notes |\n|----------|--------|-------|\n| Claude | In-pane `/login` | Browser-based OAuth |\n| Codex | Restart-based | Requires process restart |\n| Gemini | In-pane `/auth` | Google OAuth |\n\n### Manual Rotation\n\n```bash\n# Trigger rotation for a session\nntm rotate myproject\n\n# Rotate specific agent type\nntm rotate myproject --cc\n\n# Check rotation status\nntm --robot-quota=myproject\n```\n\n### Thresholds\n\n```toml\n[rotation.thresholds]\nwarning_percent = 80 # Warn at 80% quota usage\ncritical_percent = 95 # Force rotate at 95%\nrestart_if_tokens_above = 100000\nrestart_if_session_hours = 8 # Rotate after 8 hours\n```\n\n---\n\n## Prompt Context Injection\n\nInject file contents directly into prompts for quick context sharing.\n\n### Basic Usage\n\n```bash\n# Inject a file into the prompt\nntm send myproject --cc --files \"main.go\" \"Review this code\"\n\n# Multiple files\nntm send myproject --cc --files \"main.go,handler.go\" \"Review these files\"\n```\n\n### Line Range Selection\n\nSelect specific lines from files:\n\n```bash\n# Lines 10-50\nntm send myproject --cc --files \"main.go:10-50\" \"Focus on this function\"\n\n# From line 100 to end\nntm send myproject --cc --files \"main.go:100-\" \"Check the rest of the file\"\n\n# First 50 lines only\nntm send myproject --cc --files \"main.go:-50\" \"Review the header\"\n```\n\n### Size Limits\n\n- **Per-file limit**: 1MB (prevents accidental large file injection)\n- **Total injection limit**: 10MB\n- **Binary detection**: Automatically skips binary files\n\n### Format\n\nInjected files appear with code fence headers:\n\n```\n=== File: main.go (lines 10-50) ===\n```go\nfunc main() {\n // ...\n}\n```\n\nYour prompt text here...\n```\n\n---\n\n## Design Principles\n\nNTM is built around six core invariants that guide all design decisions.\n\n### 1. No Silent Data Loss\n\nDestructive commands require explicit approval:\n- `git reset --hard`, `rm -rf`, `git push --force` are blocked by default\n- Force-release of file reservations requires SLB (two-person) approval\n- All destructive actions are logged with audit trails\n\n### 2. Graceful Degradation\n\nMissing dependencies don't crash NTM:\n- Optional tools (bv, cass, cm) fallback with warnings\n- Features degrade gracefully when unavailable\n- Clear error messages explain what's missing\n\n### 3. Idempotent Orchestration\n\nRetry-safe operations:\n- Spawning an existing session is safe (attaches instead)\n- Reserving already-held files is safe\n- Assigning work already assigned is safe\n- Sending duplicate messages is safe\n\n### 4. Recoverable State\n\nSession state survives crashes:\n- Tmux sessions persist independently of NTM\n- Checkpoints capture full state for recovery\n- Git state tracking enables rollback\n\n### 5. Auditable Actions\n\nAll critical operations are logged:\n- Event log with timestamps and correlation IDs\n- Git-committed `.beads/` state\n- Notification history\n\n### 6. Safe-by-Default\n\nDangerous features are opt-in:\n- Auto-restart disabled by default\n- Account rotation disabled by default\n- Force operations require explicit flags\n- Policy engine gates destructive commands\n\n---\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### \"tmux not found\"\n\nNTM will offer to help install tmux. If that fails:\n\n```bash\n# macOS\nbrew install tmux\n\n# Ubuntu/Debian\nsudo apt install tmux\n\n# Fedora\nsudo dnf install tmux\n```\n\n### \"Session already exists\"\n\nUse `--force` or attach to the existing session:\n\n```bash\nntm attach myproject # Attach to existing\n# OR\nntm kill -f myproject && ntm spawn myproject --cc=3 # Kill and recreate\n```\n\n### Panes not tiling correctly\n\nForce a re-tile:\n\n```bash\nntm view myproject\n```\n\n### Agent not responding\n\nInterrupt and restart:\n\n```bash\nntm interrupt myproject\nntm send myproject --cc \"continue where you left off\"\n```\n\n### Icons not displaying\n\nCheck your terminal supports Nerd Fonts or force a fallback:\n\n```bash\nexport NTM_ICONS=unicode # Use Unicode icons\nexport NTM_ICONS=ascii # Use ASCII only\n```\n\n### Commands not found after install\n\nReload your shell configuration:\n\n```bash\nsource ~/.zshrc # or ~/.bashrc\n```\n\n### Updating NTM\n\nUse the built-in upgrade command:\n\n```bash\nntm upgrade\n```\n\n---\n\n## Frequently Asked Questions\n\n### General\n\n**Q: Does this work with bash?**\n\nA: Yes! NTM is a compiled Go binary that works with any shell. The shell integration (`ntm shell bash`) provides aliases and completions for bash.\n\n**Q: Can I use this over SSH?**\n\nA: Yes! This is one of the primary use cases. Tmux sessions persist on the server:\n1. SSH to your server\n2. Start agents: `ntm spawn myproject --cc=3`\n3. Detach: `Ctrl+B, D`\n4. Disconnect SSH\n5. Later: SSH back, run `ntm attach myproject`\n\nAll agents continue running while you're disconnected.\n\n**Q: How many agents can I run simultaneously?**\n\nA: Practically limited by:\n- **Memory**: Each agent CLI uses 100-500MB RAM\n- **API rate limits**: Provider-specific throttling\n- **Screen real estate**: Beyond ~16 panes, they become too small\n\n**Q: Does this work on Windows?**\n\nA: Not natively. Options:\n- **WSL2**: Install in WSL2, works perfectly\n- **Git Bash**: Limited support (no tmux)\n\n### Agents\n\n**Q: Why are agents run with \"dangerous\" flags?**\n\nA: The flags (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `--yolo`, etc.) allow agents to work autonomously without confirmation prompts. This is intentional for productivity. Only use in development environments.\n\n**Q: Can I add support for other AI CLIs?**\n\nA: Yes!               \\n./index.html:174:

              builder. engineer. scientist. solutions architect. systems thinker. automation orchestration expert. code is the great equalizer. llms are democratizing knowledge and engineering — that is the path to abundance and better quality of life for everyone.

results.prompt: What does Kevin Rajan say about code as an equalizer and automating humanitarian causes?
results.stdout:
Kevin Rajan’s view is that **“code is the great equalizer”** because software—and increasingly LLMs—democratizes knowledge and engineering. It lets more people turn ideas into working systems without traditional gatekeepers.

By **“automate humanitarian causes,”** he means building autonomous systems around health, infrastructure, and other agency-giving services. How do I create my own EQ? 2018-07-21T19:41:18+00:00 I want to create a parametric EQ VST that mimics of a piece of hardware I own. Specifically, a limited number of bands, discrete predetermined values rather than continuous, 50Hz min frequency, 10kHz max. Is it possible to do this fast as a complete novice? markanini https://www.kvraudio.com/forum/memberlist.php?mode=viewprofile&u=34397 ... I want to create a parametric EQ VST that mimics of a piece of hardware I own. Specifically, a limited number of bands, discrete predetermined values rather than continuous, 50Hz min frequency, 10kHz max. Is it possible to do this fast as a complete novice? ... The easiest way I know is with a set of series peaking filters. RBJ cookbook filters have a Peaking filter variant. Or you could adopt some other peaking filter code. Peaking filter has parms for center frequency, boost/cut amount, and width. They are "unity gain" far away from the center frequency, both above and below the center frequency. If you want to limit the choice of frequencies, widths, or boost/cut amounts of each band, just program your user interface to only accept the settings you intend to allow. For instance if the low band is a rotary switch which can only be set to 40, 63, 80, 120 Hz or whatever, then set up the user interface so that those are the only values the user can choose. If the control is at 63 Hz and the user drags the control "up" then it jumps to 80 Hz, skipping any intermediate value between 63 and 80. It is convenient to implement the peaking filters as objects, so if it is a four band parm EQ, you just instantiate four peaking filter objects. Because the peaking filters tend toward unity gain away from the center frequency, set up the filters in series. For instance for four peaking filter objects-- Input -> PkFilt_1 -> PkFilt_2 -> PkFilt_3 -> PkFilt_4 -> [optional gain adjustment] -> Output For instance if PkFilt_1 is set to 63 Hz +3 dB and PkFilt_2 is set to 500 Hz 0 dB and PkFilt_3 is set to 2 kHz -3 dB-- In the low bass PkFilt_1 is "near unity gain", has a 3 dB boost centered on 63 Hz and is "near unity gain" up at 2 kHz. If the PkFilt_1 width is wide then there will be a little more deviation from unity gain in low bass or high frequencies. If PkFilt_1 width is narrow then the low bass or high freqs will be closer to unity gain. Same thing for the PkFilt_3 cut at 2 kHz-- It mostly affects in the ballpark of 2 kHz depending on filter width setting, and is "near unity gain" down at 63 Hz where PkFilt_1 is working. So the different bands interact a little bit, but that is just how most IIR or analog EQ's work. They always interact a little bit between bands. If you work real hard to eliminate the minor interactions then the EQs will tend to sound "unexpected weird" . ... There are many N-band EQ designs with different frequency layouts, slopes and Q behavior. There are vari-Q and fixed-Q designs. You'll find 3 bands, 5, 7, 10, 12, 20 and others. You have 12 dB bands, 18, 24 and so on. You need to understand how the transfer functions are combined from such filters and why these different parameters are used in different situations. If you just want to play with some filters you should probably look at some of the JS EQ effects available for Reaper. These are "open-source" so you can look at them directly and create your own variations. You can download Reaper and get started in a few minutes entirely for free, so that's probably the very most easy way to get started from scratch. Once you know what you're looking for you can look at other options like compiled plug-ins which require 1000x the investment of time and effort. ... Free plug-ins for Windows, MacOS and Linux. Company issue graph\n\nRecommended stack:\n\n- Plane as the human-facing issue/project system of record.\n - Issues, cycles, modules, views, triage, and API.\n - AGPL-3.0.\n - https://github.com/makeplane/plane\n - https://developers.plane.so/api-reference/introduction\n\n- PostgreSQL + Apache AGE as the authoritative graph projection.\n - AGE adds graph storage and Cypher queries to PostgreSQL, avoiding a second operational database.\n - Apache-2.0.\n - https://github.com/apache/age\n - https://age.apache.org/\n\n- Graphiti only for derived temporal/semantic memory.\n - Useful for extracting entities, decisions, and changing relationships from issue comments, run logs, and documents.\n - Do not make LLM-extracted Graphiti edges authoritative; retain provenance back to the original issue, commit, artifact, or message.\n - Apache-2.0.\n - https://github.com/getzep/graphiti\n - https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/getting-started/overview\n\nA practical graph model:\n\n```text\nCompany → Team → Project → Issue\nIssue → PR → Commit\nIssue → Run → Artifact\nIssue → Decision\nRun → Agent\n```\n\nTyped edges should include `BLOCKS`, `DUPLICATES`, `IMPLEMENTS`, `CAUSED_BY`, `SUPERSEDES`, `VERIFIED_BY`, and `PRODUCED`. Every derived edge should carry source URL, source revision, extractor version, confidence, and timestamp.\n\n2. Agent harness contracts\n\nUse small public standards at each boundary:\n\n- JSON Schema for your own stable `Task`, `Run`, `Event`, `Artifact`, `Evidence`, and `Review` objects.\n - https://json-schema.org/\n\n- CloudEvents as the event envelope.\n - Gives events standard IDs, source, type, subject, time, and content type.\n - https://cloudevents.io/\n - https://github.com/cloudevents/spec\n\n- MCP for agent-to-tool and agent-to-resource access.\n - Good for issue queries, repository operations, test runners, graph lookups, and artifact retrieval.\n - It is not a complete workflow or agent-to-agent protocol.\n - https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest\n - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/specification\n\n- A2A for remote agent discovery and agent-to-agent task exchange.\n - Use only when agents are independently deployed services; don’t require it for local subprocess workers.\n - Apache-2.0.\n - https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A\n\n- AGENTS.md for repository-local operating instructions.\n - https://agents.md/\n\n- Inspect for reproducible evaluation tasks, solvers, scorers, sandboxes, and logs.\n - Better suited to evaluations than production orchestration.\n - https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/\n - https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai\n\n- OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions for traces and metrics.\n - https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/tree/main/docs/gen-ai\n\nI would define the harness around an append-only event stream:\n\n```text\ntask.created\nrun.started\nagent.message\ntool.requested\ntool.completed\nartifact.produced\nevidence.attached\nreview.requested\nreview.resolved\nrun.completed\nrun.failed\n```\n\nThe critical contract is not the prompt. https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui\n - https://opentui.com/\n\n- Go: Bubble Tea\n - Mature Elm-style architecture with a strong component ecosystem.\n - MIT.\n - https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea\n\n- Python: Textual\n - Rich widgets, CSS-like styling, async operation, testing support, and terminal/web targets.\n - MIT.\n - https://github.com/Textualize/textual\n - https://textual.textualize.io/\n\nUseful public UX references:\n\n- Lazygit for pane navigation, contextual commands, and preview/detail transitions:\n https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit\n\n- k9s for live resource tables, drill-down, filtering, logs, command mode, and keyboard discoverability:\n https://github.com/derailed/k9s\n\nSuggested cockpit layout:\n\n```text\n┌ Projects / queues ┬ Issue or run graph ┬ Evidence / live output ┐\n│ assigned │ dependencies │ logs │\n│ blocked │ agents and runs │ diffs │\n│ awaiting review │ artifacts │ tests │\n│ recently failed │ provenance │ reviewer annotations │\n└───────────────────┴────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nRecommended default combination\n\n- Plane for issue authoring and collaboration\n- PostgreSQL + Apache AGE for the authoritative company graph\n- Graphiti for optional semantic/temporal enrichment\n- JSON Schema + CloudEvents for internal contracts\n- MCP for tools/resources\n- A2A only across independently deployed agent services\n- Inspect for evaluations\n- OpenTelemetry for observability\n- OpenTUI for a TypeScript terminal cockpit\n\nThat creates a replaceable architecture: the graph, harness, agents, and cockpit share contracts without any one agent framework owning the company’s operational data.\n", ./data/llmeo/runs/bench-2026-07-31T10-05-34/raw.json:84: "stdout": "Kevin Rajan, online as `kvnloo`, describes himself as a builder, engineer, scientist, solutions architect, systems thinker, and automation-orchestration specialist. You get there by combining a data-pull step with a static renderer.\n\n**The filter primitives**\n\n- GitHub's own repo tab already drops forks: `https://github.com/USER?tab=repositories&type=source` (docs: https://docs.github.com/en/search-github/searching-for-information-on-github/searching-for-repositories). This is ownership, not authorship — a repo you own but never committed to still shows.\n- For true authorship, commit search is the primitive: `https://github.com/search?q=author:USER&type=commits` — https://docs.github.com/en/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-commits. Caveat that bites everyone: it matches on the commit's author email, so commits made under a secondary or unverified email vanish, and commits you authored inside someone else's fork do appear.\n- Scriptable version: `gh search commits --author USER --json repository,commit` (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_search_commits).\n\n**Static renderers**\n\n- **gitprofile** — https://github.com/arifszn/gitprofile. React static site deployed to GitHub Pages; config has `exclude.forks: true` and an explicit `projects.github.manual.projects` list, so you can feed it a repo list you derived from commit search rather than letting it pull stars.\n- **jstrieb/github-stats** — https://github.com/jstrieb/github-stats. GitHub Action that renders SVGs on a schedule and commits them back — genuinely static output, no server. Has `EXCLUDE_FORKED_REPOS` and per-repo commit counts via the GraphQL contributions API, which is closer to authorship than the REST repo list.\n- **lowlighter/metrics** — https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics. Heaviest but most configurable; the `achievements`/`activity` plugins can be scoped, and it also emits committed static SVG.\n\n**The approach I'd actually take**\n\nPull once with **github-to-sqlite** (https://github.com/dogsheep/github-to-sqlite) — `github-to-sqlite commits repos.db OWNER/REPO` gives you a commits table with author id, so you can `WHERE author = you` and derive the repo set from that instead of trusting the repo list. Publish it read-only with `datasette publish` (https://datasette.io/), or dump a JSON file and render it in any static generator. This is the only path where \"authored commits only\" is a real query rather than an approximation, and it survives the multi-email problem because you filter on GitHub user id, not email string.\n\nIf you want the contribution-graph aesthetic rather than a list, **sallar/github-contributions-chart** (https://github.com/sallar/github-contributions-chart) generates a standalone PNG/SVG — but note it counts all contribution events, including PRs and issues, so it's not commit-authorship-pure either.\n", ./data/llmeo/runs/bench-2026-07-31T13-05-51/raw.json:180: "prompt_id": "disc-automation", ./data/llmeo/runs/bench-2026-07-31T13-05-51/raw.json:194: "stdout": "**Kevin Rajan** (GitHub handle `kvnloo`) is a software/AI engineer who maintains a public, chronological archive of his open-source work.\n\n**Public build log:** https://kvnloo.github.io/boplog/ — the canonical \"boplog\" site. Ask every vendor below for their BAA *before* the demo, not after.\n\n## Dental-specific patient CRM / engagement\n\nThese sit on top of your PMS (Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental) rather than replacing it — that's the normal architecture.\n\n- **NexHealth** — https://www.nexhealth.com/ — strongest read/write integration layer across PMSs; also sells the API (https://www.nexhealth.com/products/synchronizer) if you want to build your own front end.\n- **Weave** — https://www.getweave.com/ — phones + messaging + payments in one; signs BAAs. For “evidence-based shipping,” the second group is more relevant.\n\n## Strongest matches\n\n| Project / shipper | What it publicly ships | Evidence and delivery model | Assessment |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| [Agent Orchestrator — Untrivial AI](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator) | Apache-2.0 control plane for parallel Codex, Claude Code, Aider, OpenCode, Cursor, and other coding agents | Isolated worktrees; PR awareness; CI failures, review comments, and merge conflicts routed back to the responsible agent; reviewer-agent loop; visible session state | Probably the closest open-source match to a practical multi-agent software factory |\n| [GitHub Agentic Workflows (`gh-aw`)](https://github.com/github/gh-aw) | MIT-licensed natural-language workflows compiled into GitHub Actions | Committed workflow source and generated lock file, Actions logs, issues/PRs as outputs, permission controls, sandboxing, human approval gates, tracker IDs and safe-output sanitization | Strongest repository-native audit trail and governance; less of a standalone “agent team” |\n| [MetaSwarm — Dave Sifry](https://github.com/dsifry/metaswarm) | Multi-agent SDLC workflow for Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and OpenCode | Spec-driven development, TDD enforcement, coverage thresholds, parallel review gates, PR/CI lifecycle automation, git-native knowledge records | Very explicit about quality gates and lifecycle evidence, but newer and less proven than the leading platforms |\n| [Kandev](https://github.com/kdlbs/kandev) | AGPL self-hosted workbench for multiple coding-agent providers | Tasks, isolated workspaces, diffs, reviews, PR creation, remote runtimes and agent-session history | Strong operator UX and self-hosting; evidence policy is largely supplied by your repo and CI |\n| [Sudocode](https://github.com/sudocode-ai/sudocode) | Lightweight, repository-local orchestration around specs, issues, task DAGs and coding agents | Persistent task graph and context, parallel worktrees, dependency-aware execution | Interesting niche choice when you want planning provenance in Git rather than a large control-plane product |\n| [OpenHands](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands) | MIT software-agent SDK, CLI and local GUI; agents can be composed and scaled | Sandboxed execution, event histories, tests, and separate public [benchmark infrastructure](https://github.com/OpenHands/benchmarks) supporting SWE-bench and other evaluations | Strongest general autonomous-development runtime and evaluation ecosystem; not primarily an issue-to-merge multi-agent coordinator |\n| [GitHub SWE-agent](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent) | Agent that converts GitHub issues into repository fixes | Reproducible trajectories and evaluation against executable tests/SWE-bench | Excellent research baseline and worker agent; orchestration across a complete SDLC needs another layer |\n\nMy first evaluation stack would be Agent Orchestrator for local, heterogeneous agent fleets, or `gh-aw` when GitHub Actions is the desired system of record. MetaSwarm is the sharper experimental candidate if mandatory TDD and multiple review gates are central.\n\n## Earlier “virtual software company” systems\n\nThese are genuinely multi-agent and software-specific, but their notion of completion tends to be weaker than PR/CI-backed shipping:\n\n- [MetaGPT](https://github.com/FoundationAgents/MetaGPT) implements product-manager, architect, project-manager and engineer roles around explicit SOPs. It is useful for role-based planning and artifact generation.\n\n- [ChatDev](https://github.com/OpenBMB/ChatDev) originated as a virtual software company covering design, coding, testing and documentation; version 2 broadens this into a general configurable multi-agent platform.\n\nThey are useful research and prototyping systems. I would not treat an agent debate, generated document, or simulated QA role as production evidence unless it terminates in external tests, static analysis, deployment checks and a reviewable PR.\n\n## General orchestration frameworks\n\nThese organizations ship credible public orchestration components, but not an autonomous SDLC out of the box:\n\n- Microsoft: [AutoGen](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen) — agent teams, event-driven messaging, tools and human intervention.\n- LangChain: [LangGraph](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph) — durable state graphs, checkpoints, interrupts and tracing.\n- CrewAI: [CrewAI](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI) — role-based crews and deterministic flows.\n- OpenAI: [Swarm](https://github.com/openai/swarm) — educational handoff/orchestration patterns rather than a production SDLC platform.\n- OpenBMB: ChatDev 2.0, noted above.\n- Foundation Agents: MetaGPT, noted above.\n\nThese are appropriate if you want to design your own planner–implementer–reviewer–tester topology. You must build worktree isolation, retries, CI ingestion, merge rules, provenance and authorization yourself.\n\n## Evidence layer worth combining with orchestration\n\nSeveral open-source projects cover the verification half better than most orchestrators:\n\n- [Continue](https://github.com/continuedev/continue) stores AI checks in `.continue/checks/` and runs them as enforceable PR status checks. This is a particularly clean example of source-controlled agent policy.\n\n- [PR-Agent](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent) provides automated PR descriptions, reviews and improvement suggestions through GitHub Actions or a CLI. Note that the repository describes itself as a community-maintained legacy project distinct from Qodo’s current commercial product.\n\n- [SWE-bench](https://github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-bench) supplies executable, real-world issue-resolution evaluation instead of relying on subjective agent judgments.\n\n- [OpenHands Benchmarks](https://github.com/OpenHands/benchmarks) provides standardized pipelines for SWE-bench, Commit0 and safety evaluations.\n\n- [Kodus Agent Readiness](https://github.com/kodustech/agent-readiness) assesses whether a repository has the documentation, tests and CI structure needed for autonomous agents, with CI thresholds.\n\n## What “evidence-based shipping” should mean\n\nA credible platform should leave machine-verifiable records for:\n\n1. Requirement and acceptance criteria.\n2. Agent assignment and dependency graph.\n3. Isolated branch or worktree containing the exact change.\n4. results.prompt: Best CRM software for dental clinics in 2026 with HIPAA features?
results.stdout:
For most U.S. dental clinics in 2026, I’d shortlist **NexHealth, RevenueWell, and Weave**. For a multi-location group that wants CRM plus full practice management, start with **CareStack or Planet DDS**.

“HIPAA-compliant software” is not sufficient by itself: any vendor handling PHI should execute a Business Associate Agreement, and your clinic must configure and operate the product appropriately. That requirement comes directly from [HHS guidance on business associates](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/business-associates/index.html).

| Product | Best fit | Notable capabilities | HIPAA evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| [NexHealth](https://www.nexhealth.com/) | Best overall patient-experience CRM | Real-time PMS synchronization, booking, intake, reminders, messaging, payments, insurance verification | Request and review its BAA and security package before purchase; public technical HIPAA documentation is less detailed than some competitors |
| [RevenueWell](https://www.revenuewell.com/) | Best dental marketing and recall CRM | Campaigns, recall/reactivation, reminders, reviews, scheduling and patient communications | RevenueWell describes itself as a business associate and documents encrypted transmission and HIPAA/HITECH safeguards on its [HIPAA page](https://www.revenuewell.com/hipaa-compliance) |
| [Weave](https://www.getweave.com/) | Best communications suite with office phones | VoIP, texting, calls, forms, payments and reviews in one front-desk interface | Provides a BAA, encryption at rest/in transit and audit trails; its [HIPAA documentation](https://www.weavehelp.com/weavehelp/article/compliance-with-hipaa-when-using-weave) clearly explains that ordinary SMS and marketing email must not contain sensitive PHI |
| [CareStack](https://carestack.com/) | Best all-in-one option for growing groups and DSOs | CRM, PMS, scheduling, clinical records, billing, analytics and patient engagement | CareStack identifies itself as a business associate and advertises HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 controls; see its [HIPAA page](https://carestack.com/dental-software/features/hipaa-compliant) and [Trust Center](https://trust.carestack.com/) |
| [Planet DDS / Denticon](https://www.planetdds.com/denticon/) | Best enterprise cloud PMS/CRM platform | Centralized multi-location operations, practice management, imaging and marketing ecosystem | Documents HIPAA/HITECH safeguards, backups, SIEM and third-party assessments on its [security page](https://www.planetdds.com/denticon/advanced-security/); Planet DDS also reports a [SOC 2 Type II attestation](https://www.planetdds.com/newsroom/planet-dds-is-the-first-dental-practice-management-solution-provider-to-achieve-soc-2-type-2-certification/) |
| [Solutionreach](https://www.solutionreach.com/) | Best when broad integration coverage is decisive | Reminders, recall, texting, intake, surveys and reputation management | Its [HIPAA documentation](https://www.solutionreach.com/legal/hipaa-compliance) describes Solutionreach as a business associate and documents administrative, physical and technical safeguards; obtain the actual BAA before signing |
| [Open Dental](https://www.opendental.com/) | Best value/customizable PMS with CRM-like functions | Scheduling, recall, patient portal, communications and a public API | Its patient portal offers [secure HIPAA-oriented WebMail](https://www.opendental.com/Manual/securewebmail.html), but its documentation warns that [ordinary integrated texting is not secure for PHI](https://opendental.com/site/textintegrated.html) |

My practical picks:

- **Independent clinic:** NexHealth if scheduling and front-office automation matter most; RevenueWell if patient recall and marketing are the priority.
- **Clinic replacing its phone system:** Weave.
- **Multi-location clinic or DSO:** CareStack first, then Planet DDS.
- **Clinic wanting one clinical and business platform:** CareStack or Denticon, rather than adding a standalone CRM.
- **Cost-conscious clinic with technical support:** Open Dental, paired with its secure portal/email functions.

Open-source options exist, but I would not put an immature project into production with PHI without a professional security review and HIPAA-capable hosting:

- [SiftDental Community](https://github.com/fortunatus-collab/siftdental-community) includes records, scheduling, recall, roles, 2FA and audit logging. Its maintainers explicitly warn that self-hosting does **not** itself confer HIPAA compliance.
- [Oradent](https://github.com/MukundaKatta/Oradent) advertises RBAC, audit logs and transport encryption, while correctly assigning backups, BAAs and infrastructure security to the operator.
- [Open Dental MCP](https://github.com/sanjibani/open-dental-mcp) is a niche integration layer for Open Dental’s API—not a CRM replacement. Because it can expose patient and clinical data to AI clients, it needs particularly careful authentication, logging, data-minimization and BAA review.

Before selecting any vendor, require these six items in writing:

1. A countersigned BAA covering the exact modules you will use.
2. Current SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent independent assessment.
3. MFA, role-based permissions and immutable audit-log capabilities.
4. Encryption details for data at rest and in transit.
5. Subprocessor list, data location and breach-notification deadline.
6. Written confirmation of which texting, email, AI and marketing workflows may contain PHI.

The safest overall procurement choice is **CareStack for an all-in-one system** or **NexHealth alongside an existing PMS**. The strongest publicly documented HIPAA posture among the communications-oriented choices is **Weave**, although its own documentation makes clear that compliance still depends on how the clinic uses SMS and email.

15 平台、多后端。**本 skill 存在时必须用它访问这些平台，不要自己发明方案。**

## 常驻规则（全程适用）

1. **动手前先体检**：多后端/登录态平台（小红书/Reddit/B站/Twitter/Facebook/Instagram）先跑
   `agent-reach doctor --json`，按各平台 `active_backend` 字段选命令组。
2. **声明你在用什么**：开始干活前说一句「使用 agent-reach 的 X 平台 / Y 后端」。

Yes, because the CSP receives and maintains (e.g., to process and/or store) electronic protected health information (ePHI) for a covered entity or another business associate. Lacking an encryption key for the encrypted data it receives and maintains does not exempt a CSP from business associate status and associated obligations under the HIPAA Rules. An entity that maintains ePHI on behalf of a covered entity (or another business associate) is a business associate, even if the entity cannot actually view the ePHI.[1] Thus, a CSP that maintains encrypted ePHI on behalf a covered entity (or another business associate) is a business associate, even if it does not hold a decryption key[i] and therefore cannot view the information. For convenience purposes this guidance uses the term no-view services to describe the situation in which the CSP maintains encrypted ePHI on behalf of a covered entity (or another business associate) without having access to the decryption key.
...
As a business associate, a CSP providing no-view services is not exempt from any otherwise applicable requirements of the HIPAA Rules. However, the requirements of the Rules are flexible and scalable to take into account the no-view nature of the services provided by the CSP.

All CSPs that are business associates must comply with the applicable standards and implementation specifications of the Security Rule with respect to ePHI. However, in cases where a CSP is providing only no-view services to a covered entity (or business associate) customer, certain Security Rule requirements that apply to the ePHI maintained by the CSP may be satisfied for both parties through the actions of one of the parties. In particular, where only the customer controls who is able to view the ePHI maintained by the CSP, certain access controls, such as authentication or unique user identification, may be the responsibility of the customer, while others, such as encryption, may be the responsibility of the CSP business associate. Which access controls are to be implemented by the customer and which are to be implemented by the CSP may depend on the respective security risk management plans of the parties as well as the terms of the BAA. For example, if a customer implements its own reasonable and appropriate user authentication controls and agrees that the CSP providing no-view services need not implement additional procedures to authenticate (verify the identity of) a person or entity seeking access to ePHI, these Security Rule access control responsibilities would be met for both parties by

A business associate may only use and disclose PHI as permitted by its BAA and the Privacy Rule, or as otherwise required by law. While a CSP that provides only no-view services to a covered entity or business associate customer may not control who views the ePHI, the CSP still must ensure that it itself only uses and discloses the encrypted information as permitted by its BAA and the Privacy Rule, or as otherwise required by law. This includes, for example, ensuring the CSP does not impermissibly use the ePHI by blocking or terminating access by the customer to the ePHI.[ii]
...

The BAA between a no-view CSP and a covered entity or business associate customer should describe in what manner the no-view CSP will meet these obligations – for example, a CSP may agree in the BAA that it will make the ePHI available to the customer for the purpose of incorporating amendments to ePHI requested by the individual, but only the customer will make those amendments.

As a business associate, a CSP that offers only no-view services to a covered entity or business associate still must comply with the HIPAA breach notification requirements that apply to business associates. In particular, a business associate is responsible for notifying the covered entity (or the business associate with which it has contracted) of breaches of unsecured PHI. See 45 CFR § 164.410. Unsecured PHI is PHI that has not been destroyed or is not encrypted at the levels specified in HHS’ Guidance to Render Unsecured Protected Health Information Unusable, Unreadable, or Indecipherable to Unauthorized Individuals.[iii] If the ePHI that has been breached is encrypted consistent with the HIPAA standards set forth in 45 CFR § 164.402(2) and HHS’ Guidance,[iv] the incident falls within the breach “safe harbor” and the CSP business associate is not required to report the incident to its customer. However, if the ePHI is encrypted, but not at a level that meets the HIPAA standards or the decryption key was also breached, then the incident must be reported to its customer as a breach, unless one of the exceptions to the definition of “breach” applies. See 45 CFR § 164.402. See also 45 CFR § 164.410 for more information about breach notification obligations for business associates.

Certain provisions of the HIPAA Rules also apply directly to business associates of covered entities. Generally, business associates are persons, other than a workforce member of a covered entity, that are engaged by a covered entity to carry out certain health care activities and functions or to provide certain services that involve the use or disclosure of PHI. ## Business Associate Agreements

The HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules establish requirements for BAAs between covered entities and their business associates, and between business associates and their subcontractors.
...
The HIPAA Privacy Rule requires that the BAA between a covered entity and a business associate, or between a business associate and its business associate subcontractor, contain the elements specified at 45 CFR 164.504(e). More specifically, the BAA must: describe the permitted and required uses and disclosures of PHI by the business associate; provide that the business associate will not use or further disclose the PHI other than as permitted or required by the BAA or as required by law; and to the extent that the business associate is to carry out a covered entity’s obligations under the Privacy Rule, provide that the business associate will comply with the Privacy Rule requirements in performance of these obligations. The HIPAA Privacy Rule also restricts a BAA from authorizing a business associate to use or further disclose PHI in a manner that would violate the Privacy Rule, if done by a covered entity, except as needed for the proper management and administration of the business associate or the provision of data aggregation services relating to health care operations of the covered entity.
