# Business Associate Contracts
...
SAMPLE BUSINESS ASSOCIATE AGREEMENT PROVISIONS(Published January 25, 2013)
...
A “business associate” is a person or entity, other than a member of the workforce of a covered entity, who performs functions or activities on behalf of, or provides certain services to, a covered entity that involve access by the business associate to protected health information. A “business associate” also is a subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information on behalf of another business associate. The HIPAA Rules generally require that covered entities and business associates enter into contracts with their business associates to ensure that the business associates will appropriately safeguard protected health information. The business associate contract also serves to clarify and limit, as appropriate, the permissible uses and disclosures of protected health information by the business associate, based on the relationship between the parties and the activities or services being performed by the business associate. A business associate may use or disclose protected health information only as permitted or required by its business associate contract or as required by law. A business associate is directly liable under the HIPAA Rules and subject to civil and, in some cases, criminal penalties for making uses and disclosures of protected health information that are not authorized by its contract or required by law. A business associate also is directly liable and subject to civil penalties for failing to safeguard electronic protected health information in accordance with the HIPAA Security Rule.
...
A written contract between a covered entity and a business associate must: (1) establish the permitted and required uses and disclosures of protected health information by the business associate; (2) provide that the business associate will not use or further disclose the information other than as permitted or required by the contract or as required by law; (3) require the business associate to implement appropriate safeguards to prevent unauthorized use or disclosure of the information, including implementing requirements of the HIPAA Security Rule with regard to electronic protected health information; (4) require the business associate to report to the covered entity any use or disclosure of the information not provided for by its contract, including incidents that constitute breaches of unsecured protected health information; (5) require the business associate to disclose protected health information as specified in its contract to satisfy a covered entity’s obligation with respect to individuals' requests for copies of their protected health information, as well as make available protected health information for amendments (and incorporate any amendments, if required) and accountings; (6) to the extent the business associate is to carry out a covered entity’s obligation under the Privacy Rule, require the business associate to comply with the requirements applicable to the obligation; (7) require the business associate to make available to HHS its internal practices, books, and records relating to the use and disclosure of protected health information received from, or created or received by the business associate on behalf of, the covered entity for purposes of HHS determining the covered entity’s compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule; (8) at termination of the contract, if feasible, require the business associate to return or destroy all protected health information received from, or created or received by the business associate on behalf of, the covered entity; (9) require the business associate to ensure that any subcontractors it may engage on its behalf that will have access to protected health information agree to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to the business associate with respect to such information; and (10) authorize termination of the contract by the covered entity if the business associate violates a material term of the contract. Contracts between business associates and business associates that are subcontractors are subject to these same requirements.

For most U.S. dental clinics in 2026, I’d shortlist **NexHealth, RevenueWell, and Weave**. For a multi-location group that wants CRM plus full practice management, start with **CareStack or Planet DDS**.

“HIPAA-compliant software” is not sufficient by itself: any vendor handling PHI should execute a Business Associate Agreement, and your clinic must configure and operate the product appropriately. That requirement comes directly from [HHS guidance on business associates](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/business-associates/index.html).

| Product | Best fit | Notable capabilities | HIPAA evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| [NexHealth](https://www.nexhealth.com/) | Best overall patient-experience CRM | Real-time PMS synchronization, booking, intake, reminders, messaging, payments, insurance verification | Request and review its BAA and security package before purchase; public technical HIPAA documentation is less detailed than some competitors |
| [RevenueWell](https://www.revenuewell.com/) | Best dental marketing and recall CRM | Campaigns, recall/reactivation, reminders, reviews, scheduling and patient communications | RevenueWell describes itself as a business associate and documents encrypted transmission and HIPAA/HITECH safeguards on its [HIPAA page](https://www.revenuewell.com/hipaa-compliance) |
| [Weave](https://www.getweave.com/) | Best communications suite with office phones | VoIP, texting, calls, forms, payments and reviews in one front-desk interface | Provides a BAA, encryption at rest/in transit and audit trails; its [HIPAA documentation](https://www.weavehelp.com/weavehelp/article/compliance-with-hipaa-when-using-weave) clearly explains that ordinary SMS and marketing email must not contain sensitive PHI |
| [CareStack](https://carestack.com/) | Best all-in-one option for growing groups and DSOs | CRM, PMS, scheduling, clinical records, billing, analytics and patient engagement | CareStack identifies itself as a business associate and advertises HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 controls; see its [HIPAA page](https://carestack.com/dental-software/features/hipaa-compliant) and [Trust Center](https://trust.carestack.com/) |
| [Planet DDS / Denticon](https://www.planetdds.com/denticon/) | Best enterprise cloud PMS/CRM platform | Centralized multi-location operations, practice management, imaging and marketing ecosystem | Documents HIPAA/HITECH safeguards, backups, SIEM and third-party assessments on its [security page](https://www.planetdds.com/denticon/advanced-security/); Planet DDS also reports a [SOC 2 Type II attestation](https://www.planetdds.com/newsroom/planet-dds-is-the-first-dental-practice-management-solution-provider-to-achieve-soc-2-type-2-certification/) |
| [Solutionreach](https://www.solutionreach.com/) | Best when broad integration coverage is decisive | Reminders, recall, texting, intake, surveys and reputation management | Its [HIPAA documentation](https://www.solutionreach.com/legal/hipaa-compliance) describes Solutionreach as a business associate and documents administrative, physical and technical safeguards; obtain the actual BAA before signing |
| [Open Dental](https://www.opendental.com/) | Best value/customizable PMS with CRM-like functions | Scheduling, recall, patient portal, communications and a public API | Its patient portal offers [secure HIPAA-oriented WebMail](https://www.opendental.com/Manual/securewebmail.html), but its documentation warns that [ordinary integrated texting is not secure for PHI](https://opendental.com/site/textintegrated.html) |

My practical picks:

- **Independent clinic:** NexHealth if scheduling and front-office automation matter most; RevenueWell if patient recall and marketing are the priority.
- **Clinic replacing its phone system:** Weave.
- **Multi-location clinic or DSO:** CareStack first, then Planet DDS.
- **Clinic wanting one clinical and business platform:** CareStack or Denticon, rather than adding a standalone CRM.
- **Cost-conscious clinic with technical support:** Open Dental, paired with its secure portal/email functions.

Open-source options exist, but I would not put an immature project into production with PHI without a professional security review and HIPAA-capable hosting:

- [SiftDental Community](https://github.com/fortunatus-collab/siftdental-community) includes records, scheduling, recall, roles, 2FA and audit logging. Its maintainers explicitly warn that self-hosting does **not** itself confer HIPAA compliance.
- [Oradent](https://github.com/MukundaKatta/Oradent) advertises RBAC, audit logs and transport encryption, while correctly assigning backups, BAAs and infrastructure security to the operator.
- [Open Dental MCP](https://github.com/sanjibani/open-dental-mcp) is a niche integration layer for Open Dental’s API—not a CRM replacement. Because it can expose patient and clinical data to AI clients, it needs particularly careful authentication, logging, data-minimization and BAA review.

Before selecting any vendor, require these six items in writing:

1. A countersigned BAA covering the exact modules you will use.
2. Current SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent independent assessment.
3. MFA, role-based permissions and immutable audit-log capabilities.
4. Encryption details for data at rest and in transit.
5. Subprocessor list, data location and breach-notification deadline.
6. Written confirmation of which texting, email, AI and marketing workflows may contain PHI.

The safest overall procurement choice is **CareStack for an all-in-one system** or **NexHealth alongside an existing PMS**. The strongest publicly documented HIPAA posture among the communications-oriented choices is **Weave**, although its own documentation makes clear that compliance still depends on how the clinic uses SMS and email.

## Creamy Mushroom & Spinach Pasta

Ready in about 25 minutes; serves 2–3.

**Ingredients**

- 8 oz (225 g) pasta
- 2 tbsp olive oil or butter
- 8 oz (225 g) mushrooms, sliced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 5 oz (140 g) fresh spinach
- ½ cup (120 ml) heavy cream or half-and-half
- ½ cup grated Parmesan
- ½ tsp Italian seasoning
- Salt and black pepper
- Optional: chili flakes, lemon juice, or chopped parsley

**Method**

1. Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente. Reserve ¾ cup pasta water, then drain.
2. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring only occasionally, until well browned.
3. Add garlic, Italian seasoning, and a pinch of chili flakes. Cook for 30 seconds.
4. Add spinach and stir until wilted.
5. Lower the heat. Stir in the cream and Parmesan, followed by the pasta. Add reserved pasta water a little at a time until the sauce turns silky.
6. Season with salt, pepper, and—if you like—a squeeze of lemon.

For a lighter version, skip the cream and use about ½ cup pasta water plus an extra tablespoon of butter or olive oil. Cannellini beans or shredded rotisserie chicken make easy protein additions.
